items.title: The canonical morphism from the normalised to the associated chain complex is a quasi-isomorphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file simplicial.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-quasi-isomorphism at source lines 4144-4152: for a simplicial object V of an abelian category the canonical morphism N(V) to s(V) is a quasi-isomorphism, equivalently the complement D(V) of the previous lemma is acyclic. The proof at source lines 4154-4202 is a double induction: it first notes the result for the objects K(A,k), then states the hypothesis IH_{n,m} for simplicial objects concentrated in degrees at least m, observes that IH_{n,n} is trivial, and in the induction step splits V through the skeleton inclusion K(V_m,m) = i_{m!} sk_m V into a short exact sequence whose quotient W is concentrated in degrees at least m+1, uses the induced morphism of short exact sequences of the complexes N and s (which needs both exactness lemmas) and the long exact sequence to deduce the statement for V from its ends. The bookkeeping of the two induction indices and the identification of the quotient are the substance; the statement itself is one line.
